about: Old Home Distillers is a family farm distillery in Lebanon, Madison County, in the hills southeast of Syracuse. Jerry and Marlene Carvell founded it in 2015, converting a hundred-year-old stable on historic Campbell Road into a stillhouse, and their sons Aaron and Adam help run it. As a New York State farm distillery it works only with New York-grown ingredients and never buys bulk spirit, so every drop is mashed, fermented and distilled on the farm.

Empire is Old Home’s American single malt: a whiskey made entirely from New York-grown malted barley at a single distillery, distilled in the family’s copper pot stills and aged in oak. It is bottled at 86 proof. American single malt grew up as a category in the last decade, and Empire is a farm-scale, all-New York take on a style more often associated with Scotland. The distillery describes biscuit, ale and butterscotch notes with an aromatic lift, and suggests it on the rocks or in a Rob Roy.
